c.tagline: South Africa's jacaranda-shaded administrative capital of monuments and embassies.

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis are uncommon; most visitors use Uber or Bolt, or arrange a metered cab by phone. Agree a fare before any unmetered ride.

emergency.note: 112 from a mobile phone reaches emergency services; 10111 is the police flying squad and 10177 is the ambulance/medical line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution in the CBD/Sunnyside at night; standard SA crime precautions

hood_desc: The stately government-and-embassy quarter below the Union Buildings, dotted with jacaranda-lined avenues, the National Zoological Gardens and grand hotels; the natural base for first-time visitors who want landmarks on the doorstep.

A lively student district around the University of Pretoria and the Gautrain station, packed with bars, cafes, hostels and nightlife; suits younger and budget travellers who want to be out and social.

A leafy, upmarket suburb centred on Brooklyn Mall and Nieuw Muckleneuk, full of restaurants, coffee shops and boutiques; favoured by families and business travellers wanting comfort and easy shopping.
One of Pretoria's most exclusive residential areas, a quiet enclave of large homes, embassies and tree-lined streets on the eastern ridges; good for a calm, secure stay away from the bustle.
A modern commercial hub around the vast Menlyn Park mall and Menlyn Maine precinct, with hotels, cinemas and a casino; convenient for shoppers and anyone based on the city's east side.

water.note: Tap water in Pretoria is generally safe to drink.

transit.hours: The Gautrain runs roughly 05:30-20:30; A Re Yeng BRT and Tshwane buses run daytime into early evening; minibus taxis run all day but thin out after dark.
transit.note: Pretoria mixes the modern Gautrain rapid rail (to Johannesburg and OR Tambo Airport) and the A Re Yeng bus rapid transit with the ubiquitous minibus taxis and municipal Tshwane buses; ride-hailing fills the gaps, and there is no metro.
transit.pay: The Gautrain uses a rechargeable tap Gold Card; A Re Yeng and Tshwane buses use their own smart cards; minibus taxis are cash only.

bus: Intercity coaches (Intercape, Greyhound, City to City)

transit.m: Gautrain from OR Tambo to Hatfield/Pretoria (~45 min, every 12-30 min)
Metered taxi or e-hailing to central Pretoria (45-60 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; a service charge is often added automatically for larger groups.

food.name: Braai and boerewors
food.desc: Wood-fire grilling is a national ritual. The coil of coriander-spiced beef sausage goes on first, then chops and steak, with pap and chakalaka alongside.

places.name: Rocket 88 Bar and Braai
places.note: Braai-focused kitchen with a second branch in Moreleta Park; strong on grilled meat.

places.name: Bra.i
places.note: Built around South African meat culture: skilpadjies, venison potjie, big portions.

places.name: Hazel Food Market
places.note: Saturday market with wors rolls cooked over coals and local producers on every stall.

food.name: Bobotie
food.desc: Cape Malay baked mince, curried and sweetened with dried fruit and chutney under a set savoury custard, served with yellow rice, raisins and sambals.

places.name: Karoo Cattle & Land
places.note: Steakhouse chain that keeps proper bobotie and boerewors on the traditional menu.

places.name: Die Kospotte
places.note: Afrikaans buffet of home cooking: bobotie, potjiekos and braai, three hours at the table.

places.name: Bra.i
places.note: Serves bobotie beside lamb tripe and other genuinely old-school Afrikaans plates.

food.name: Biltong and droewors
food.desc: Air-dried beef or game cured with coriander, vinegar and salt, sliced thick and wet or shaved dry. Droewors is the thin dried sausage version.

places.name: Boeremark
places.note: Pretoria's Saturday farmers market, running before dawn; the heartland for biltong and rusks.

places.name: Capital Craft Beer Academy
places.note: Deep-fried biltong as a bar snack, an unusual twist worth ordering with a beer.

places.name: Hazel Food Market
places.note: Several curers sell kudu and beef biltong to taste before you buy.

food.name: Vetkoek
food.desc: Deep-fried dough balls, split and stuffed with curried mince, or eaten sweet with syrup and grated cheese. Cheap, filling and utterly Highveld.

places.name: Boeremark
places.note: Stalls fry them from 5am; the classic pairing is vetkoek with mince and coffee.

places.name: Die Kospotte
places.note: Buffet keeps a vetkoek station alongside the pots of stew.

places.name: Harrie's Pancakes
places.note: Family cafe near the Union Buildings doing vetkoek and pancakes all day.

food.name: Pap en wors met chakalaka
food.desc: Stiff white maize porridge with grilled sausage and a spicy tomato, bean and carrot relish. The plate that crosses every community in Gauteng.

places.name: Bra.i
places.note: Pap, roosterkoek and chakalaka served as standard sides with the grill.

places.name: Marabastad food stalls
places.note: Historic trading quarter where street kitchens do pap and wors at township prices.

places.name: Die Kospotte
places.note: Pap and relish on the buffet next to potjie and braai meat.

food.name: Koeksisters
food.desc: Plaited dough deep-fried then plunged into ice-cold syrup so it stays crunchy outside and drips inside. The Cape Malay koesister is spiced and coconut-rolled.

places.name: Boeremark
places.note: Bakers here are the reference standard; buy a box early before they sell out.

places.name: Hazel Food Market
places.note: Weekend bakers sell both the Afrikaans and Cape Malay versions side by side.

places.name: Die Kospotte
places.note: Dessert table always has koeksisters and melktert at the end of the buffet.

food.name: Rooibos tea
food.desc: Caffeine-free red bush tea grown only in South Africa, drunk plain, with milk, or iced. Often served with a slice of melktert in the afternoon.

places.name: Cafe Riche
places.note: Pretoria's oldest cafe, on the historic square since 1905; good for a slow pot of tea.

places.name: Blue Crane Restaurant
places.note: Terrace overlooking the bird sanctuary dam; a long-standing Pretoria tea and lunch spot.

places.name: Hazel Food Market
places.note: Local blenders sell loose rooibos and honeybush to take home.

food.name: South African craft beer
food.desc: Gauteng has a busy microbrewery scene, from crisp weiss beers to dark ales, poured in beer gardens made for long, hot afternoons.

places.name: Capital Craft Beer Academy
places.note: The city's craft-beer landmark, with one of the country's widest local tap lists.

places.name: Brauhaus am Damm
places.note: German-style brewery and beer garden by the water, a short drive north-east.

places.name: Cockpit Brewhouse
places.note: Microbrewery in the historic diamond village, easy to pair with a mine tour.

landmarks: Union Buildings
Herbert Baker's sandstone crescent of government crowns Meintjieskop above terraced gardens, watched over by a nine-meter bronze of a beaming Mandela.
Voortrekker Monument
This massive granite memorial to the Boer Great Trek features a marble historical frieze and a cenotaph struck by a sunbeam each December 16.
Church Square
Pretoria's historic heart gathers the Palace of Justice, the Old Raadsaal and a brooding statue of Paul Kruger amid shaded lawns.
Kruger House Museum
The modest Victorian home of President Paul Kruger preserves the Boer leader's furniture, state coach and the stone lions gifted by Barney Barnato.
Freedom Park
A contemplative hilltop memorial complex honors those who died in South Africa's conflicts, its Wall of Names and eternal flame facing the Voortrekker Monument.
Pretoria National Botanical Garden
A quartzite ridge splits this tranquil garden of cycads, aloes and half of South Africa's tree species, with weekend concerts on the lawns.
National Zoological Garden
South Africa's national zoo spans 85 riverside hectares of enclosures, explored on foot, by golf cart or from the aerial cableway overhead.
Melrose House
The ornate Victorian mansion where the treaty ending the Anglo-Boer War was signed in 1902 retains its stained glass and period furnishings.
Jacaranda Streets in October
Each spring some 70,000 jacarandas ignite the capital in purple bloom, best photographed in Groenkloof and from the Union Buildings' lawns.
Ditsong National Museum of Natural History
Home of Mrs Ples, the famous Australopithecus skull from Sterkfontein, this grand old museum showcases the Cradle of Humankind's fossil treasures.

train.note: No scheduled international trains - the cross-border services to Zimbabwe and Mozambique have long been suspended, and Rovos Rail (https://rovos.com/) and the Blue Train (https://www.bluetrain.co.za/), both of which start from Pretoria, are luxury holiday journeys rather than transport. The Gautrain rapid rail links Pretoria with Centurion, Sandton, Johannesburg and OR Tambo airport in under an hour, and Shosholoza Meyl runs slow long-distance services to Johannesburg, Polokwane, Musina and Cape Town.

bus.note: Most cross-border coaches originate in Johannesburg and pick up in Pretoria, so check whether your service starts here. Intercape is the main operator; Harare takes about 16 hours via Beitbridge, where waits of several hours are normal. Carry your passport and book online. Domestic coaches to Polokwane, Nelspruit and Durban run from the Pretoria station forecourt.

ferry.note: Pretoria is inland on the Highveld with no navigable water, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Cullinan
half.blurb: Historic diamond-mining town 40 minutes east, home of the Cullinan Diamond mine with surface and underground tours.

half.name: Johannesburg
half.blurb: South Africa's biggest city, an hour south by Gautrain, for the Apartheid Museum, Constitution Hill and Soweto.

half.name: Hartbeespoort Dam
half.blurb: Resort dam in the Magaliesberg foothills ~45 min west, with an aerial cableway, boat cruises and craft markets.

full.name: Pilanesberg National Park
full.blurb: Big Five game reserve in an ancient volcanic crater about 2.5 hours northwest, next to Sun City.

full.name: Sun City
full.blurb: Sprawling casino, golf and waterpark resort complex ~2 hours away in North West province.
